title: Farol Protocol v0.1 — widget/get
description: Request and response envelopes for the widget/get method. See protocol/SPEC.md §5.2 for the normative polling model. The core calls this once per refresh cycle, per widget declared in the handshake result (protocol/SPEC.md §6.3) - the plugin MUST NOT push widget data unsolicited. This file also defines GitRepository and RemoteStatus; it references ActionDeclaration from handshake.schema.json.

widget_id.description: Must match the `id` of a WidgetDeclaration returned by this plugin's handshake/hello result.

RemoteStatus.title: RemoteStatus
RemoteStatus.description: Discriminated union on `kind`. "no_remote" is a distinct serialization from a tracked repo reporting 0 ahead / 0 behind - the core never has to infer "no remote" from an absent field.

ahead.description: Commits ahead of the configured upstream.

GitRepository.title: GitRepository
GitRepository.description: One repository item reported by widget/get.

id.description: Stable identifier - the repository's absolute filesystem path.

name.description: Short display name (e.g. the directory name).

dirty.description: true = working tree has pending changes; false = clean.

remote_status.description: MUST be kind="no_remote" if and only if this repository's corresponding fetch ActionDeclaration has enabled=false (protocol/SPEC.md invariant carried over from data-model.md).

WidgetItem.title: WidgetItem
WidgetItem.description: Pairs one GitRepository with its corresponding fetch ActionDeclaration. This is how the actions[] list, possibly empty at handshake time, reaches the core in practice (protocol/SPEC.md §6.3.1).

widget_id.description: Echoes the widget_id from the request.

items.description: MAY be empty - a configured scan root with no repositories under it is a valid state, not an error.

WidgetGetResponseError.title: WidgetGetResponseError
WidgetGetResponseError.description: E.g. code -32004 / reason "scan_root_unreadable" when the configured root exists but cannot be read. A pointwise error here does not, by itself, mark the plugin connection unavailable - the core keeps the last known items (protocol/SPEC.md §5.2).
